content.text: I always am getting the following build error in fcrepo-mint when executing:
...on a local copy of PR-705. Does it work for you?
Works for me as well for Travis CI:
Hm: "ERROR 13:40:22.128 (ContainerWrapper) Error with test server java.net.BindException: Address already in use (Line 689)"
1- The error message above complains about an occupied address. Sure there is no other build in parallel or anything?
2- Sometimes local Maven artifacts that got installed during development of other modules interfere. Did you try to build with a clean Maven repo?
3- Which Java Version do you use? Oracle JDK 7 as in Travis?

When I build, there is no other build running in parallel, but I have Tomcat running on 8080 for other reasons. This is the purpose of the build-helper-maven-plugin, it ensures that the integration tests do not clash with bound ports.
When I stop my Tomcat, your PR succeeds.

It appears that the defaults that you are introducing in this PR override the ports that the build-helper-maven-plugin selects. A requirement of this ticket would be to figure out a way to have defaults not override the build-helper-maven-plugin.

Ok, I think I see the problem: The default I choose for `fcrepo.test.port` is `8080` because in all the places where this property is queried there is `8080` as default, in case the property is not set. This now interferes with the build-helper-maven-plugin configuration.
Solution might be to set fcrepo.test.port empty by default: `<fcrepo.test.port/>`
Can you try this with your setup?
Did `<fcrepo.test.port/>` work for you as intended?
Instead some NPE happens during verify phase:
[INFO] Fedora Repository Object Serialization Module ..... SUCCESS [2.995s]
[INFO] Fedora Repository HTTP Commons Module ............. SUCCESS [3.708s]

[INFO] Fedora Repository Deployable Web Application ...... FAILURE [7.191s]
[INFO] Fedora Repository LDP integration tests Module .... SKIPPED
[INFO] Fedora Repository RDF integration tests Module .... SKIPPED
No idea what's going on here. :-/
Now, I think I know what's going on.

The Build Helper Maven Plugin dynamically creates Maven properties on runtime in the `process-test-classes` phase. One of these properties is `fcrepo.test.port` [1]. There are more port parameters in other configurations in other POMs. It seems like this plugin is crashing if the property already exists and is empty (bug?).

I'm not sure what to do here. Since Maven has no problems it doesn't look like there is anything broken. It's just IntelliJ IDEA complaining about undefined properties. My pull request, however, makes no sense then.
Are these port properties documented somewhere?
The referenced ports are internal to the build framework, and not documented specifically. Plugin details are available here:
If it would be helpful, please feel free to add a page under:
The build-helper-maven-plugin dynamically changes the environment in a way IDEs might not be aware of. That's a problem of IDEs Maven support, not a problem of the build system itself.

I propose renaming those dynamic properties to denote the fact that they are generated at build time, e.g. `dynamic.fcrepo.test.port`. Does this make sense? If you think so I will update the pull request accordingly and add a page to the Developer Guide.
Changing the property names of the dynamically generated ports would be for developer clarity, not for any function purpose, correct?
If so, I would suggest the name be: "fcrepo.dynamic.test.port", "fcrepo.dynamic.jms.port", and "fcrepo.dynamic.stomp.port"
Additionally, you will want to update these and similar ports in the related and child projects:
> Changing the property names of the dynamically generated ports would be for developer clarity, not for any function purpose, correct?
> If so, I would suggest the name be: "fcrepo.dynamic.test.port", "fcrepo.dynamic.jms.port", and "fcrepo.dynamic.stomp.port"
> Additionally, you will want to update these and similar ports in the related and child projects:
Yep, this is already on the list.
, please use the button, "Start Work", if you are working this ticket (as you clearly are). Then click "Start Review" when you are done.
There is no such button for me. :-/
May be I need to be assigned?
This module doesn't use dynamic properties:
I had some trouble testing fcrepo-module-auth-xacml, fcrepo-webapp-plus and fcrepo4-release-tests locally. TravicCI runs where ok.

I ran into the same thing with fcrepo-module-auth-xacml recently – the issue for me was that it depends on fcrepo-module-auth-rbacl, so you need to do a full mvn install on the rbacl module before trying to verify the xacml build. (mvn verify won't do it).
, This looks good... once the minor comment in the fcrepo4 PR is addressed and the fcrepo4-release-tests build is fixed.
All PRs have been merged into their respective master branches:

A couple of system properties are referenced throughout the POMs and code but never declared in any POM. These properties can be set in Maven command line executions: ```mvn ... -Dfcrepo.test.port=8080```
The properties should be declared in the man POM using some default values. They can than be overridden by command line arguments.
